newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds says regrets pension transfer errors.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds says regrets pension transfer errors.

text.p: Lloyds Bank, part of Lloyds TSB Group Plc, said on Tuesday it regrets the errors in its pensions transfer business which have led to the bank being fined 350,000 stg by industry regulator IMRO.

"Lloyds Bank deeply regrets the errors which have resulted in charges being brought against it by IMRO for its pension transfer business between April 1988 and June 1993," the bank said in a statement.
Lloyds said it has identified some 2,600 pension transfer customers of which it anticipates having to pay compensation to around 1,500.
As a group, Lloyds TSB has made provisions totalling 165 million stg for possible compensation payments to do with the mis-selling of pension products.
These relate to the Lloyds Bank business as well as the pensions activities of TSB, before it merged with Lloyds last year, and of Lloyds' insurance subsidiary Lloyds Abbey Life.
Lloyds said it would fully compensate customers for any losses.
It said its procedures had been fully overhauled three years ago to ensure that other customers would not be similarly affected in future. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
